words.meaning: Practical wisdom or intelligence, especially in the context of moral virtue.
words.sentence1: His leadership required not just technical knowledge, but deep phronesis to navigate the ethical dilemma. (His leadership required not just technical knowledge, but deep practical wisdom to navigate the ethical dilemma.)
words.sentence2: Ancient Greek philosophers considered phronesis to be the most vital virtue for a good ruler. (Ancient Greek philosophers considered practical wisdom to be the most vital virtue for a good ruler.)

words.meaning: Moderation, restraint, and prudence in actions or speech.
words.sentence1: El sabio aconsejó actuar con mesura frente a las provocaciones. (The wise person advised acting with moderation in the face of provocations.)
words.sentence2: Su discurso demostró gran mesura y madurez intelectual. (His speech demonstrated great restraint and intellectual maturity.)

words.meaning: The ability to judge well; perception and philosophical insight.
words.sentence1: Il faut beaucoup de discernement pour distinguer l'illusion de la vérité. (It takes a lot of discernment to distinguish illusion from truth.)
words.sentence2: Le philosophe a analysé la situation avec un grand discernement. (The philosopher analyzed the situation with great insight.)

words.meaning: A particular philosophy or view of life; a world view.
words.sentence1: Seine philosophische Weltanschauung wurde von Immanuel Kant geprägt. (His philosophical worldview was shaped by Immanuel Kant.)
words.sentence2: Jede Kultur entwickelt im Laufe der Zeit ihre eigene Weltanschauung. (Every culture develops its own worldview over the course of time.)

words.meaning: Deep wisdom, supreme intelligence, or divine intellect.
words.sentence1: Jinrui wa sono eichi o kashite konnan o norikoeta. (Humanity used its deep wisdom to overcome the difficulty.)
words.sentence2: Kodai no tetsugakusha-tachi wa fukai eichi o motteita. (The ancient philosophers possessed profound wisdom.)

words.meaning: Sound judgment, discretion, and philosophical discernment.
words.sentence1: Ci vuole grande giudizio per comprendere la natura umana. (It takes great sound judgment to understand human nature.)
words.sentence2: Le sue parole riflettevano il giudizio di un vecchio saggio. (His words reflected the judgment of an old wise man.)

words.meaning: Philosophy, or the study of fundamental truths about knowledge and existence.
words.sentence1: Dongfang zheshi zaiyu xunhuan he ziran de hexie. (Eastern philosophy lies in the harmony between cycles and nature.)
words.sentence2: Ta yi sheng de jingli yanjiu gudaide zheshi. (He spent his life studying ancient philosophy.)

words.sentence1: Socrateseun seyang cheolhakui giyoseowotda. (Socrates was the foundation of Western philosophy.)
words.sentence2: Insaengui uimireul chatneun geotcheoreom cheolhakeun jungyohada. (Just like finding the meaning of life, philosophy is important.)

words.meaning: Philosophy, or deep intellectual doctrine and wisdom.
words.sentence1: Korsphea-sa-vada chea kruosrea samkhan knongkar kit. (Studying philosophy is important for thinking.)
words.sentence2: Avey del anak ningkitchea roop-bap phea-sa-vada? (What you are thinking is a philosophical form?)

words.meaning: Philosophy; the love and pursuit of wisdom.
words.sentence1: Die antieke Grieke het die fondamente van die wysbegeerte gelê. (The ancient Greeks laid the foundations of philosophy.)
words.sentence2: Wysbegeerte help ons om krities oor die lewe na te dink. (Philosophy helps us to think critically about life.)
